input: # W1. A pointer is read on the document as it is written (Decision 27).
# A member the reference has beside it is the one a pointer through
# it names, though a 3.0 reference does not apply it.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"T":{"properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T","properties":{"x":{"type":"integer"}}},"P":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"}}}}
# Where a step is missing at a reference, the pointer is read on in
# what the reference names, and the row says which it was read through.
{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"T":{"properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"P":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"}}}}
# The same in 3.1, where the reference has a member beside it that the
# pointer does not name.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"T":{"properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T","description":"d"},"P":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"}}}}
# Through two references in turn.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"T":{"properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}},"B":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B"},"P":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"}}}}
# Through a reference that names nothing, and through one into another
# document: nothing is there to read on in.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Nope"},"P":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"},"E":{"$ref":"other.yaml#/T"},"Q":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/E/properties/x"}}}}

input: # `strict` holds to RFC 6901, which finds nothing where a step is
# missing: the lenient step raises.
{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"T":{"properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"P":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"}}}}
# The root is where a pointer starts. It is never read through, though
# `slots: 'all'` makes it a reference here.
{"openapi":"3.0.3","$ref":"#/x-a","x-a":{"y":{"type":"string"}},"components":{"schemas":{"P":{"$ref":"#/y"}}}}
# W2. A schema that references its own `$defs`, and a reference to it:
# the usual shape of a bundled schema. Neither is a cycle.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"S":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/S/$defs/inner","$defs":{"inner":{"type":"string"}}},"R":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/S"}}}}
# A schema that references its own member.
{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/p","properties":{"p":{"type":"string"}}}}}}
# A member of a reference whose own target is missing.
{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Missing","properties":{"p":{"type":"string"}}},"P":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/p"}}}}
# A reference from inside a reference to a member beside it.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"T":{"type":"object"},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T","properties":{"a":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/b"},"b":{"type":"integer"}}}}}}
# A loop of pointers, each read through the other, names nothing but
# itself: both are cut, and under `cycles: 'keep'` too.
{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B/x"},"B":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/y"}}}}
{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B/x"},"B":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/y"}}}}
# W3. A region the object model gives no type takes the type of the
# reference that lands on it, so the references inside it are read.
# Into an extension:
{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"S":{"$ref":"#/x-defs/T"},"N":{"type":"string"}}},"x-defs":{"T":{"properties":{"n":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/N"}}}}}
# Into `definitions` in a 3.1 schema, which 2020-12 does not have:

{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"Account":{"properties":{"id":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Account/definitions/accountId"}},"definitions":{"accountId":{"properties":{"t":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Type"}}}}},"Type":{"type":"string"}}}}
# Into a 3.0 component whose name the pattern refuses:
{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"My Schema":{"properties":{"n":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/N"}}},"R":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/My%20Schema"},"N":{"type":"string"}}}}
# A region typed by a reference may hold the reference that types the
# next: each is a round.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"S":{"$ref":"#/x-a/T"},"N":{"type":"string"}}},"x-a":{"T":{"properties":{"n":{"$ref":"#/x-b/U"}}}},"x-b":{"U":{"properties":{"m":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/N"}}}}}
# A reference that is data types nothing. Under `slots: 'all'` the
# reference inside what it names is read all the same, as data: the
# member beside it is not applied, as a 3.1 schema's would be.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"N":{"type":"string"}}},"x-a":{"p":{"$ref":"#/x-b/U"}},"x-b":{"U":{"properties":{"m":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/N","description":"d"}}}}}
# The same region, named by a schema: it is a schema, and the member is
# applied.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"N":{"type":"string"},"S":{"$ref":"#/x-b/U"}}},"x-b":{"U":{"properties":{"m":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/N","description":"d"}}}}}
# A mapping value names a schema too, though it is no reference and
# nothing is put in its place. What it lands on is a schema, so the
# references in a schema that only a mapping value names are read. The
# name of a schema component is a name, and types nothing.

{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"Pet":{"discriminator":{"propertyName":"kind","mapping":{"dog":"#/x-models/Dog","cat":"Cat"}}},"Cat":{"type":"object"},"Name":{"type":"string"}}},"x-models":{"Dog":{"properties":{"name":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Name"}}}}}
# Under `refs: 'pointer'` nothing is typed by what lands on it, and the
# reference is data.

{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"Pet":{"discriminator":{"propertyName":"kind","mapping":{"dog":"#/x-models/Dog","cat":"Cat"}}},"Cat":{"type":"object"},"Name":{"type":"string"}}},"x-models":{"Dog":{"properties":{"name":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Name"}}}}}
# The schema a mapping value names may hold the mapping value that
# types the next: each is a round, as with a reference.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"discriminator":{"propertyName":"k","mapping":{"b":"#/x-b/B"}}},"Leaf":{"type":"string"}}},"x-b":{"B":{"discriminator":{"propertyName":"k","mapping":{"c":"#/x-c/C"}}}},"x-c":{"C":{"properties":{"p":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Leaf"}}}}}
# The default mapping of 3.2 is one too.

{"openapi":"3.2.0","components":{"schemas":{"Pet":{"discriminator":{"propertyName":"k","defaultMapping":"#/x-m/Other"}},"N":{"type":"string"}}},"x-m":{"Other":{"properties":{"n":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/N"}}}}}
# A place takes the type of the first to land on it, a reference or a
# mapping value, in the order of the document. Here a response's
# reference is first, so the place is a response, and the reference in
# it is where a response has no member: it is data.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"responses":{"R":{"$ref":"#/x-u/T"}},"schemas":{"S":{"discriminator":{"propertyName":"k","mapping":{"t":"#/x-u/T"}}},"N":{"type":"string"}}},"x-u":{"T":{"description":"d","properties":{"n":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/N"}}}}}
# With the mapping value first the place is a schema, the reference in
# it is read, and the response's reference lands on a schema, which
# its row says.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"S":{"discriminator":{"propertyName":"k","mapping":{"t":"#/x-u/T"}}},"N":{"type":"string"}},"responses":{"R":{"$ref":"#/x-u/T"}}},"x-u":{"T":{"description":"d","properties":{"n":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/N"}}}}}
# A reference that names nothing, in a schema that only a mapping
# value names, is reported as in any schema.

{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"Pet":{"discriminator":{"propertyName":"k","mapping":{"dog":"#/x-models/Dog"}}}}},"x-models":{"Dog":{"properties":{"gone":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Nope"}}}}}
# The order of the report: a reference is listed when the walk first
# comes to it, and a pointer that only passes one does not come to it.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"P":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"},"M":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Nope"},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Gone","properties":{"x":{"type":"integer"}}}}}}
# A reference into another document: its URI, against the base in
# force, and its fragment.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"other.yaml#/components/schemas/X"},"B":{"$ref":"https://example.org/defs.json"},"C":{"$ref":"common/types.yaml#Thing"}}}}
# W6. Nesting and references past `maxDepth` raise this package's code.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"k0":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k1"},"k1":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k2"},"k2":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k3"},"k3":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k4"},"k4":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k5"},"k5":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k6"},"k6":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k7"},"k7":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k8"},"k8":{"type":"string"}}}}

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"k0":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k1"},"k1":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k2"},"k2":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k3"},"k3":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k4"},"k4":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k5"},"k5":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k6"},"k6":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k7"},"k7":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/k8"},"k8":{"type":"string"}}}}
# A pointer read through more references than `maxDepth` raises it too:
# each of these is read through the one after it, and nothing here is
# nested deeper than five.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"A12":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A11/not"},"A11":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A10/not"},"A10":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A9/not"},"A9":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A8/not"},"A8":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A7/not"},"A7":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A6/not"},"A6":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A5/not"},"A5":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A4/not"},"A4":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A3/not"},"A3":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A2/not"},"A2":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A1/not"},"A1":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A0/not"},"A0":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"T":{"not":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"}}}}}
# Written the other way about, each is read before the next asks for
# it, and nothing is deep. The row lists the references this pointer was
# itself read through: what each of those was read through is in its
# own row.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"T":{"not":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"}},"A0":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"A1":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A0/not"},"A2":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A1/not"},"A3":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A2/not"}}}}
# The same pointers under `cycles: 'keep'`: where a reference lands is
# the same fact, whatever shape the tree is asked in.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"T":{"properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T","properties":{"x":{"type":"integer"}}},"P":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"},"Q":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/y"},"B":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"R":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B/properties/x"}}}}

# `inline-once` puts a value at the first reference to land on it,
# however each is written: the second here is read through a reference
# to the same place, and is kept as written.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"T":{"properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"P1":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T/properties/x"},"P2":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"}}}}
# The connections report reads the same landings. A locator through a
# Path Item `$ref` finds an operation the named item has, and one the
# referring item has beside its `$ref`.

{"openapi":"3.1.0","paths":{"/a":{"$ref":"#/components/pathItems/P","put":{"responses":{}}},"/l":{"get":{"responses":{"200":{"description":"ok","links":{"viaRef":{"operationRef":"#/paths/~1a/get"},"beside":{"operationRef":"#/paths/~1a/put"},"none":{"operationRef":"#/paths/~1a/post"}}}}}}},"components":{"pathItems":{"P":{"get":{"responses":{}}}}}}
# A mapping value is a pointer too. One that is read on through a
# reference says where it lands, as a reference's own row does.

{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"T":{"properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}},"P":{"discriminator":{"propertyName":"k","mapping":{"m":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x","direct":"#/components/schemas/T/properties/x"}}}}}}
# An operationId that two routes reach is reported whatever shape the
# tree is asked in: under `inline-once` the second route's `$ref` stays
# as written in the tree, and is a route all the same.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","paths":{"/a":{"$ref":"#/components/pathItems/P"},"/b":{"$ref":"#/components/pathItems/P"}},"components":{"pathItems":{"P":{"get":{"operationId":"shared","responses":{}}}}}}
# A Path Item's own fields beside its `$ref` are on its routes, with
# those of the item it names.

{"openapi":"3.1.0","paths":{"/a":{"$ref":"#/components/pathItems/P","post":{"operationId":"dup","responses":{}}},"/b":{"post":{"operationId":"dup","responses":{}}},"/c":{"get":{"operationId":"shared","responses":{}}}},"components":{"pathItems":{"P":{"get":{"operationId":"shared","responses":{}}}}}}
# Under `slots: 'all'` a `$ref` where the model puts an operation is a
# reference, and it is on a route as any other is.
{"openapi":"3.0.3","paths":{"/a":{"get":{"$ref":"#/x-operation"}},"/b":{"get":{"$ref":"#/x-operation"}}},"x-operation":{"operationId":"shared","responses":{}}}
# A name in a region that only a reference types is a connection.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","paths":{"/a":{"get":{"operationId":"getA","responses":{"200":{"$ref":"#/x-responses/Ok"}}}}},"x-responses":{"Ok":{"description":"ok","links":{"self":{"operationId":"getA"},"lost":{"operationId":"nope"}}}}}
# A reference inside members that its own reference dropped is in no value
# of the tree. It is a site all the same, and is reported as what it is.
{"openapi":"3.0.0","components":{"schemas":{"P":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T","properties":{"x":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Missing"}}},"T":{"type":"string"}}}}
# Under `slots: 'all'` the root is a site where it has a `$ref`. One that
# names nothing is left as written, at the place whose pointer is empty, and
# every pointer still starts at the root as written.
{"openapi":"3.0.0","paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B"},"B":{"type":"string"}}},"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Nope"}
# And one that names a schema is that schema: the tree is what it names.
{"openapi":"3.0.0","paths":{},"components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B"},"B":{"type":"string"}}},"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B"}
# A pointer past a reference that was cut reads the document as written:
# the member beside the reference is there, and one that is not is not
# found. Neither is cut for passing a cut reference.

{"openapi":"3.0.0","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B","properties":{"x":{"type":"integer"}}},"B":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A"},"there":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"},"gone":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/y"}}}}
# The order of the reports. Under the default a landing is entered at its
# first reference, so `B` is reported before `M`, which the document has
# before it.
{"openapi":"3.0.0","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B"},"M":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Nope"},"B":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Gone"}}}}
# A reference that reaches its own container through another reference is
# cut, whichever of the two the walk meets first: both are left as written,
# and neither is reported resolved while it holds its map as written.
{"openapi":"3.0.0","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/C/properties/q"},"C":{"properties":{"q":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/C"}}}}}}
{"openapi":"3.0.0","components":{"schemas":{"C":{"properties":{"q":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/C"}}},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/C/properties/q"}}}}
# Every site is listed, in walk order, with what became of it: one that
# names a reference left as written is left as that one is, one whose `$ref`
# is no string is left, and one whose pointer comes back to itself is cut.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B"},"B":{"$ref":"#/nope"},"C":{"$ref":42},"D":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/D/x"}}}}
# What each reference of an earlier row names, by the `sites` column: a
# reference whose `$ref` is no string names nothing.
{"openapi":"3.1.0","components":{"schemas":{"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/B"},"B":{"$ref":"#/nope"},"C":{"$ref":42},"D":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/D/x"}}}}

# another reference: then the two columns part.

{"openapi":"3.0.3","components":{"schemas":{"T":{"properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}},"A":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T"},"direct":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/T/properties/x"},"through":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/A/properties/x"},"gone":{"$ref":"#/components/schemas/Nope"},"other":{"$ref":"other.yaml#/X"}}}}
